title: Add model-tier evaluation harness for primary DM and auditor roles
description:
Claude-vs-Codex comparison is mostly curiosity and is confounded by runtime changes like `l3b3`. The practical model question is which model tier is required for each Eshyra role. Evaluate primary DM and auditor roles independently, especially within the same provider, and measure total accepted-turn cost/usage rather than just per-call token counts.

Acceptance criteria:

- Define a short deterministic scenario that can be run under multiple primary DM / auditor model pairings on the same commit.
- Use deterministic roll fixtures for combat comparison, not live RNG.
- Scenario should include Sela / village-authority dialogue; asking what happened; asking what to expect if investigating; traveling to the watchtower; lighting a torch / entering the hollow; goblin ambush; at least one player attack; at least one enemy attack; a save/check or death save in the deterministic fixture.
- Support evaluating primary DM and auditor roles independently: fixed primary DM + varied auditor; fixed auditor + varied primary DM.
- Suggested staged matrix: Phase 1 holds primary DM constant and varies auditor with Opus + Haiku, Opus + Sonnet, Opus + Opus as a ceiling/control only if useful, GPT-5.5 + GPT-5.4-mini, and GPT-5.5 + stronger GPT auditor tier if available; Phase 2 holds best auditor constant and varies primary DM with Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku if available and GPT-5.5 vs lower GPT primary tiers if available; Phase 3 evaluates cheapest viable pairings such as Sonnet + Haiku, Sonnet + Sonnet, and lower GPT primary + mini auditor if available.
- Capture comparison metrics: first-pass audit accept rate; primary DM retry count; auditor call count; total expensive primary-DM calls per accepted player turn; auditor rejection causes; auditor false rejects; auditor false accepts; JSON/parse failures; tool correctness; player-visible roll compliance; combatant-state correctness; unsupported inference rate; qualitative prose/style notes; approximate usage by primary DM vs auditor.
- Explicitly test the hypothesis that a stronger auditor may reduce total usage by avoiding false rejects and expensive primary-DM retries.
- Document that prior Claude-vs-Codex comparisons were confounded by `l3b3` and differing session content.
- Output should make it easy to compare table feel separately from mechanical correctness.
notes: PR #309 opened for model-tier evaluation harness. Validation passed: targeted model evaluation/profile/combat fixture tests and npm run verify:worktree.
close_reason: Merged PR #309 with model-tier evaluation harness, deterministic scenario/matrix, metrics aggregation, tests, and docs.
